claims.text: In Pulumi, a package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside a package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories so that each repository contains one package, and this improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), each versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply semver Git tag, then run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
The Pulumi IDP Private Registry exists at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/ and is the target of `pulumi package publish`.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed, which violates semver.
In a package with unrelated ComponentA and ComponentB, an enhancement to ComponentA bumps the package to v1.1.0 and a breaking change to ComponentB bumps it to v2.0.0 under semver.
